summary: @servicetitan/microfront-auth ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated math_init.js payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/... and then invokes the downloaded Bun binary against a sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a ~721KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle (string-array shuffle routine, custom base-alphabet decoder, randomized identifiers, '// @bun @bun-cjs' header) whose name does not describe its contents and whose behavior is not derivable from the source. The Bun-runtime detour bypasses Node-based scanners and Node-level sandboxing. The payload runs unconditionally on every npm install with no user consent. The dist/ files present a small plausibly-legitimate auth library that provides cover for the top-level dropper. The package is published under the @servicetitan npm scope with repository.url pointing at the placeholder github.com/servicetitan/playground.git, consistent with a scope-impersonation or scope-compromise release rather than a legitimate ServiceTitan library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
